test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 on right- and left-hand variants; verify inboard/outboard angles are applied relative to the vehicle side of mounting.

text: Front/rear position lamps (A, R1, R2) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard; reduced angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify unobstructed apparent surface over 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20°/80° below H-plane if H-plane < 750 mm).

text: Front/rear position lamps (A, R1, R2) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below; 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1 at the declared mounting height: verify vertical angles 15°/15° (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm; 5°/15° if > 2,100 mm).

text: Front/rear position lamps singular (MA, MR) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 80° inboard / 80° outboard.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 80°/80° horizontal visibility.

text: Front/rear position lamps singular (MA, MR) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 10° below, or 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 15°/10° vertical (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm).

text: Front/rear position lamps pair (MA, MR) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 20° inboard / 80° outboard.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 20°/80° horizontal visibility.

text: Front/rear position lamps pair (MA, MR) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 10° below, or 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 15°/10° vertical (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm).

text: Stop lamps (S1, S2) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard; reduced angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard may be used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 45°/45° horizontal (20°/45° below H-plane if H-plane < 750 mm).

text: Stop lamps (S1, S2) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below; 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 15°/15° vertical (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm; 5°/15° if > 2,100 mm).

text: Stop lamps singular (MS) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 45°/45° horizontal visibility.

text: Stop lamps singular (MS) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 10° below, or 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 15°/10° vertical (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm).

text: Stop lamps pair (MS) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard / 45° outboard.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 0°/45° horizontal visibility.

text: Stop lamps pair (MS) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 10° below, or 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit), outer lens, housing
test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 15°/10° vertical (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm).

text: Unless specified otherwise, the light intensity in the various directions of measurement shall meet the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, these values being mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis (on the vehicle horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference).
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement relative to the reference axis and centre of reference at the grid points of the applicable Annex 3 figure; pass if each measured intensity >= the figure's percentage × required minimum, rounded down to three significant digits.

text: Where front and rear direction indicator lamps, front and rear position lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, parking lamps, stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS, or side marker lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp; mounting
test_case: Check the manufacturer-declared mounting height (H plane); if <= 750 mm, verify photometric intensity down to V = 5° down only; pass if all points from 5° down upward meet the minimums.

text: Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern should be substantially uniform, i.e. the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp; reversing lamp
test_case: Scan intensity between grid points of the applicable figure; pass if every intermediate direction >= the lowest minimum value on the surrounding grid lines.

text: In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of a lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
applies_to: Reversing lamp
test_case: Visual examination of the lit reversing lamp; if local variations appear, measure intensity between adjacent measuring directions of Figure A3-V; pass if every value >= 50 % of the lower of the two prescribed minimums.

text: Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c, 12 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp
test_case: Photometric measurement at the Figure A3-I grid points; pass if each intensity >= the stated percentage of the minimum required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 for the respective function.

text: Stop lamps of category S3 and S4 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-III as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 7).
applies_to: Stop lamp
test_case: If the stop lamp is category S3 or S4: photometric measurement at the Figure A3-III grid points; pass if each intensity >= the stated percentage of the Table 7 minimum.

text: Reversing lamps shall meet, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference (H = 0°, V = 0°, on the vehicle horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference), the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.
applies_to: Reversing lamp
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the reversing lamp at the Figure A3-V measuring points; pass if each intensity >= the cd value shown in Figure A3-V.

text: In any test of conformity carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used with the consent of the competent authority responsible for approval tests, the manufacturer being responsible for proving that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
applies_to: Photometric and colorimetric test methods
test_case: Where alternative methods are used, check documented authority consent and equivalence/correlation evidence; pass if both exist.

text: The conformity requirements of mass-produced lamps shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
applies_to: Housing, outer lens, retro-reflector, reflector, fasteners (mechanical/geometric conformity)
test_case: CoP inspection: measure mechanical and geometric features of randomly selected production lamps against approved drawings; pass if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

text: With respect to photometric performance, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (photometry)
test_case: Photometric test per paragraph 4.8. on a randomly selected production lamp; pass if no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced lamps shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Outer lens / emitted light colour of rear position, stop and reversing lamps
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of randomly selected production lamps under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.; pass if chromaticity coordinates are within the prescribed limits.

text: The approval marking arrangement of the lamp (single light signalling lamp, or grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, or a lens intended to be used in different types of lamps) shall be made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation; the arrangements shown in Annex 7 are examples only and any other arrangement made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. is acceptable.
applies_to: Approval marking on the rear combination lamp (outer lens / housing): rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of the marking on the lamp against paragraph 3.3. and the Annex 7 examples. Pass if the marking shows the approval mark (E-number and approval number), the regulation references with series of amendments (e.g. 148R-01, 150R-01) and the function symbols (e.g. R/R2, S/S2, AR, retro-reflector class IA). Any required horizontal arrow for side-specific mounting, or for the side meeting photometry up to 80° H, shall also be present.

text: A light source module shall bear an identification code consisting of 'MD' followed by the approval mark (E-number) and the approval number of the lamp with which it has been approved (e.g. MD E3 17325).
applies_to: LED modules on PCB (light source modules for rear position, stop and reversing functions)
test_case: Visual inspection of each light source module. Pass if the identification code 'MD' + E-number + lamp approval number is present and matches the approval of the lamp.

text: For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements. The luminous intensity distribution after 1 and after 10 minutes of operation may be calculated from the distribution measured after photometric stability by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 minute, after 10 minutes and after photometric stability has occurred.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function unit), LED modules on PCB
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp from cold switch-on at 1 min and 10 min (directly, or scaled from the stabilized distribution by the HV ratios); pass if all test points are within the min/max intensity limits at both times.

text: For all lamps other than reversing and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements. The luminous intensity distribution after 1 min of operation may be calculated from the distribution after 30 min of operation or after photometric stabilization by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 min and after 30 min or after photometric stabilization.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit), Stop lamp (function unit), LED modules on PCB
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of rear position and stop functions at 1 min and at 30 min or after photometric stability (direct, or 1 min distribution scaled by HV ratio); pass if all test points are within the min/max limits.

text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the front and rear position lamp shall additionally be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate; the distribution at that point in time may be calculated from the distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit)
test_case: Measure intensity at HV at 4 s after switch ON and scale the paragraph 1 distribution; pass if all test points meet the min/max requirements (deemed compliant for LED-only per paragraph 2.1.2).

text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the stop lamp shall additionally be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate; the distribution at that point in time may be calculated from the distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit)
test_case: Measure intensity at HV at 0.2 s after switch ON and scale the paragraph 1 distribution; pass if all test points meet the min/max requirements (deemed compliant for LED-only per paragraph 2.1.2).

text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the reversing lamp shall additionally be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate; the distribution at that point in time may be calculated from the distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function unit)
test_case: Measure intensity at HV at 0.2 s after switch ON and scale the paragraph 1 distribution; pass if all test points meet the min/max requirements (deemed compliant for LED-only per paragraph 2.1.2).

text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, Stop lamp, Reversing lamp, LED modules on PCB
test_case: Confirm by design documentation that each function uses LED light sources only; pass if paragraph 1.2 measurements are compliant.

text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. or, the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; Outer lens; Housing
test_case: Drawing/sample inspection: verify a reserved marking area of sufficient size exists for UI or approval marking plus paragraph 3.3.4.2. markings.

text: All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; Outer lens; Housing markings
test_case: Visual inspection for legibility; indelibility check (e.g. rub test with water/solvent cloth); pass if markings remain legible.

text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value for "a" defined in Table 1; the arrangement of the markings may follow the examples shown in Annex 10.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking
test_case: Measure approval mark dimensions against Table 1 value of "a"; compare layout with Annex 10.

text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection of marking on sample: circle with "E" and country number present.

text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., placed close to the approval mark.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection: 4–6 digit sequential number present and located adjacent to the approval mark, matching the approval number.

text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection: class identification symbol per paragraph 3.2.5. present and correct for the approved class.

text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection: "150R" followed by two-digit series of amendments present.

text: The approval marking as defined in paragraph 3.3.2. may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; where used, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking
test_case: If UI used: visual comparison of mark with Figure I format; UI number matches UN database entry.

text: Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of sample for applicant trade name or mark.

text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Review manufacturer's prescribed rotation angles; if orientation ambiguous, verify "TOP" inscribed horizontally at highest part of illuminating surface.

text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of device: approval marking/UI, trade name and TOP marking (where required) legible.

text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1. and 3.3.6.1.2. are met.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector)
test_case: Inspect combined lamp marking: single mark contains sequential number/UI and conditions 3.3.6.1.1–3.3.6.1.2 satisfied.

text: Where a single approval mark is used on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp; Outer lens; Housing
test_case: Install lamp on vehicle/representative fixture; verify single approval mark visible.

text: Where a single approval mark is used on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
applies_to: Outer lens; Retro-reflector; Housing
test_case: Design review/disassembly: verify each light-transmitting part cannot be removed without removing the approval mark (e.g. mark on outer lens).

text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp approval marking
test_case: Measure mark components; compare against the minimum sizes of each pertinent UN Regulation; pass if not below the smallest required.

text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Production samples tested to the photometric, colorimetric and other requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5.; pass if samples meet all requirements and conform to the approved type.

text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflecting device; the requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (passive conspicuity); installation on M1 vehicle
test_case: Document and design review against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes (series of amendments in force at application) for the rear retro-reflector on category M1: e.g. installation position (height, lateral, distance to edge), geometric visibility angles, orientation, number and colour. Pass: all requirements verifiable at device approval are met.

text: Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Design review and conformity tests of UN R150 (photometric, environmental and durability tests); device keeps meeting photometric requirements after the tests.

text: Retro-reflective devices must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection and design/manufacturing review of samples; no defect affecting operation or maintenance found.

text: The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens, housing, fasteners/clips
test_case: Manual dismantling attempt without tools on the assembled lamp; retro-reflector components cannot be easily separated.

text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens
test_case: Inspection of the outer surface and cleaning trial with cloth; surface can be easily cleaned.

text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens
test_case: Visual and tactile inspection of the outer surface; surface smooth and any protuberances do not hinder cleaning.

text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, housing, seal/gasket
test_case: Inspection of the assembled lamp as mounted on the vehicle; inner (reflecting) surface of the retro-reflector is not accessible in normal use.

text: Retro-reflectors may consist of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, which must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens
test_case: Design review and manual separation attempt on retro-reflector with filter; optical unit and filter cannot be separated under normal use conditions.

text: The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens (colour definition)
test_case: Material/process documentation review and inspection; colour obtained in the material (e.g. tinted plastic), no paint or varnish used.

text: For testing the night-time colour of white, red or amber retro-reflective devices, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (passive conspicuity)
test_case: Colorimetric test set-up check: CIE Standard Illuminant A source, divergence angle 1/3°, illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or Annex 4, Part 1, para. 1.1 angle if a colourless surface reflection occurs); pass if the test geometry and illuminant conform.

text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of a white, red or amber retro-reflective device shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (passive conspicuity)
test_case: Illuminate with CIE Standard Illuminant A, divergence 1/3°, β1 = β2 = 0° (or Annex 4, Part 1, para. 1.1 angle); measure chromaticity x,y of reflected light with a spectroradiometer/colorimeter; pass if within the UN R48 night-time colour boundaries for the device colour (e.g. red).

text: White retro-reflective devices must not produce a selective reflection, that is to say, the trichromatic coordinates "x" and "y" of Standard Illuminant "A" used to illuminate the retro-reflective device must not undergo a change of more than 0.01 after reflection by the retro-reflective device.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (passive conspicuity)
test_case: For a white retro-reflector: measure x,y of Standard Illuminant A incident light and of light reflected by the device under the 4.2.1.2 geometry; pass if |Δx| ≤ 0.01 and |Δy| ≤ 0.01.

text: For testing the daytime colour, the retro-reflective material shall be illuminated by the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a) as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (passive conspicuity)
test_case: Daytime colorimetric test per Annex 4, Part 2: CIE D65 illumination with (45a:0) or (0:45a) geometry; pass if test conditions conform and measured daytime chromaticity is within the applicable limits.

text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of shape and dimensions per Annex 5 on all ten samples; pass if all Annex 5 requirements are met.

text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 and colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. in the sequence of Table 4; pass if RI and colour limits of 5.1.4. and 5.1.5. are met.

text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; outer lens; housing
test_case: Run the physical/mechanical tests of Table 4 (heat, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time, weathering); pass if each test and subsequent inspections are satisfactory.

text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. after each test group (trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt); pass if within R48 night-time colour limits.

text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have an RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0° after each test group; pass if RI ≥ Table 3 value.

text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of Class IA and IB red retro-reflectors at angle of divergence α = 20' must be equal to or greater than 3.00∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.00∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 1.00∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20' at the three illumination angles; pass if RI ≥ listed values.

text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of Class IA and IB red retro-reflectors at angle of divergence α = 1°30' must be equal to or greater than 5∙100 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.8∙100 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 2.5∙100 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 1°30' at the three illumination angles; pass if RI ≥ listed values.

text: The RI values of Class IA and IB white retro-reflectors must be equal to or greater than: at α = 20', 1.20∙103 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = β2 = 0°, 8.00∙102 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, 4.00∙102 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°; at α = 1°30', 2.0∙101, 1.12∙101 and 1.0∙101 mcd∙lx-1 respectively.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4; pass if RI ≥ listed values for white.

text: The RI values of Class IA and IB amber retro-reflectors must be equal to or greater than: at α = 20', 7.50∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = β2 = 0°, 5.00∙102 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, 2.50∙102 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°; at α = 1°30', 1.25∙101, 7∙100 and 6.25∙100 mcd∙lx-1 respectively.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4; pass if RI ≥ listed values for amber.

text: RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometric scan within the bounded solid angle; pass if no RI below the applicable Table 3 values for β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0° and β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.

text: Where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; installation on vehicle
test_case: If declared mounting height of H plane < 750 mm, limit downward photometric verification to 5°; pass if Table 3 values met in that range.

text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; outer lens
test_case: Measure trichromatic coordinates of reflected flux per paragraph 4.2.1.; pass if within R48 night-time red (amber/white) limits.

text: The conformity requirements for retro-reflective devices shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Dimensional and visual inspection of production samples against the approved type; pass if deviations stay within inevitable manufacturing deviations and the Regulation's requirements.

text: With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if, when testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometric measurement of a randomly chosen production retro-reflector per R150 methods; pass if no measured value is more than 20 per cent below the prescribed minimum values.

text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples per R150; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed limits.

text: In any test of conformity carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used with the consent of the Type Approval Authority, the manufacturer being responsible for proving that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Where alternative methods are used, check for documented Type Approval Authority consent and equivalence evidence (correlation data).

text: The conformity requirements of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; Housing
test_case: Dimensional and mechanical inspection of randomly selected production samples against approved drawings; pass if deviations are within inevitable manufacturing deviations.

text: With respect to photometric performance, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if, when testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation; retro-reflective devices with apparent defects are disregarded.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometric measurement of a randomly chosen production retro-reflector per the Regulation's photometric procedure; pass if no value is more than 20 % below the prescribed minimum (devices with apparent defects excluded).

text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; Outer lens
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples; pass if chromaticity coordinates are within the limits prescribed by the Regulation.

text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Rotate unmarked device about reference axis at β1 = β2 = 0° (or paragraph 5 angle), α = 20'; find minimum RI; pass if minimum RI ≥ paragraph 5 value.

text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°, and the RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Rotate TOP-marked device ±5° about its axis at β1 = β2 = 0°, α = 20'; pass if RI ≥ prescribed value at every position.

text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Verify source calibrated to CIE Standard Illuminant A (≈2856 K) and measurement per Annex 4 Part 1.

text: During photometric measurements of retro-reflective devices, stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Inspect test set-up for masking of stray reflections.

text: The light source and photometer head should remain stable throughout the period of the test, the laboratory ambient temperature should not vary significantly, and sufficient time should be allowed for the apparatus to stabilize before commencing measurements.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Record warm-up time, source/photometer stability and ambient temperature during test.

text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; Outer lens
test_case: Visual inspection from an observation distance of 10 m: the illuminating surface shape is not easily confused with the triangular shape of Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors.

text: The shape of the light emitting surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Class IVA shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (if Class IVA)
test_case: Visual inspection per Annex 5 paragraph 3.3 from an observation distance of 10 m: the light emitting surface shape is not easily confused with the triangular shape of Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors.

text: The light emitting surface of the retro-reflective device of Class IVA must be at least 25 cm2.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (if Class IVA)
test_case: Measure the light emitting surface area of the Class IVA retro-reflector; pass if area >= 25 cm2.

text: Compliance of retro-reflective devices of Class IVA with the shape and dimension specifications of Annex 5 paragraphs 3.1 and 3.2 shall be verified by visual inspection.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (if Class IVA)
test_case: Perform visual inspection of the Class IVA device shape and light emitting surface; pass if paragraphs 3.1 and 3.2 are met.

text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (moulded plastics reflector)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1: condition the retro-reflector for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C; record conditioning log showing compliance with durations and temperatures, then examine per para. 3.

text: After the resistance to heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, optical component
test_case: Following the heat conditioning of Annex 6 Part 1, visually inspect the retro-reflective device and its optical component; pass if no cracking and no appreciable distortion is visible.

text: After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; outer lens; seal / gasket
test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.2: after immersion sequence, inspect reflecting surface; pass if no water has reached the reflecting surface.

text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the water penetration test.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.2: visual inspection after immersion; any clearly visible water inside the optical unit = fail.

text: As an alternative to the standard water penetration test, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture test and the dust test of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied to retro-reflective devices of Classes IB and IIIB.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: If the manufacturer selects the alternative route, perform both the moisture test (para. 2) and the dust exposure test (para. 2.3) on the Class IB/IIIB retro-reflector. Pass: both tests are completed and passed.

text: The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating platform, 100 mm high with a minimum inside diameter of 140 mm.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Calibrate the spray with the specified collector. Pass: the precipitation rate is between 2.5 and 4.1 mm/min.

text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate) and 55 min OFF.
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp; reversing lamp; LED modules on PCB
test_case: Energise the rear position, stop and reversing functions at design voltage on a 5 min ON / 55 min OFF cycle. Pass: the cycle is applied throughout the test.

text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp
test_case: Check the test log. Pass: 12 h duration with 12 complete cycles.

text: Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation, and no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or be formable by tapping or tilting the device.
applies_to: Housing; outer lens; seal / gasket; retro-reflector
test_case: Inspect the interior, then tap and tilt the device. Pass: no standing pool of water is present or formed.

text: The test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Check the dust certification. Pass: fine powdered cement per ASTM C 150-84.

text: The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Check the agitation log. Pass: 2–15 s bursts every 15 min over 5 h, with settling between bursts.

text: Retro-reflective devices must be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Corrosion test per Annex 6 Part 4 (ISO 9227:2017 saline mist); afterwards verify photometric (RA) and colorimetric characteristics remain within prescribed limits.

text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; rear combination lamp assembly
test_case: Remove all removable parts from the combined lamp; expose to saline mist 24 h, dry 2 h, expose 24 h (50 h total); record exposure timing.

text: In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; Reflector; Fasteners / clips
test_case: Verify salt spray chamber at 35 °C ± 2 °C with 5 % NaCl solution by weight in distilled water with ≤ 0.02 % impurities.

text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; rear combination lamp assembly
test_case: Visual inspection immediately after 50 h saline mist test; pass if no excessive corrosion liable to impair device efficiency.

text: After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: After 48 h recovery, measure RA per Annex 6 Part 2 at β2 = 5°, α = 20'; pass if RA ≥ Table 9 minimum and ≤ Table 10 maximum.

text: After about five minutes following the wipe with the fuel test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
applies_to: Retro-reflector; outer lens
test_case: Annex 7 Part 1, para. 1.1(b): about 5 min after the wipe, inspect visually. Pass: no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are acceptable.

text: The approval number shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking (outer lens / housing)
test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark on the retro-reflective device against Annex 10, Figure A10-I: approval number located adjacent to the circled "E".

text: The digits constituting the approval number shall face the same way as the "E".
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking (outer lens / housing)
test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark: approval number digits oriented in the same direction as the letter "E".

text: The group of symbols indicating the class shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.
applies_to: Retro-reflector approval marking (class symbol)
test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark per Annex 10, Figure A10-I: class symbol (e.g. IA, IB) positioned diametrically opposite the approval number relative to the circled "E".

text: The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation: housing, fasteners / clips, seal / gasket, mounting on vehicle rear
test_case: Inspect the installation on the vehicle and run a vibration / durability evaluation under normal conditions of use (para. 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1., 2.3.10.2.). Then re-check the photometry, colour and geometric visibility of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector. Pass if the lamp stays securely mounted and all prescribed characteristics remain met.

text: It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp mounting: fasteners / clips, housing, rear position, stop and reversing lamp function units
test_case: Inspect the mounting and fixing means, then apply normal handling, operational loads and vibration. Pass if the lamp position and orientation cannot change unintentionally without deliberate use of tools, and the aim and orientation are unchanged after the test.

text: For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector; housing and fasteners (installation orientation)
test_case: Measure the angle between each function's reference axis and the vehicle's bearing plane on the road, with the lamp installed on the vehicle; pass if the axis is parallel within ±3°.

text: The reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle in the case of all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector; housing mounting
test_case: Measure the angle between each function's reference axis and the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, with the lamp installed on the vehicle; pass if the axis is parallel within ±3°.

text: The reference axis of side retro-reflectors and of side-marker lamps when fitted to the vehicle shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (only if used as a side retro-reflector); installation
test_case: Measure the angle between the reference axis of any side retro-reflector or side-marker lamp and the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, with the device installed on the vehicle; pass if the axis is perpendicular within ±3°.

text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer of the light-signalling device shall be complied with.
applies_to: Housing, fasteners/clips, seal/gasket; installation on vehicle
test_case: Inspect the installation against the manufacturer's fitting instructions; pass if all specified fitting instructions are met.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).
applies_to: Housing; installation of left/right rear combination lamps (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflector)
test_case: Vehicle installation inspection/measurement: measure lateral positions of the exterior geometrical form of left and right lamps relative to the median longitudinal plane; pass if mirror-symmetric within measurement tolerance.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
applies_to: Housing; Outer lens; left- and right-hand lamp variants
test_case: Compare left and right lamp external geometry (CAD/visual inspection); pass if exterior shapes are mirror images about the median longitudinal plane (interior structure excluded).

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
applies_to: Outer lens; LED modules; rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions; retro-reflector
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of each function on left and right lamps per the applicable device regulation; pass if both lamps of the pair meet the same colour requirements (red for rear position/stop/retro-reflector, white for reversing).

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
applies_to: LED modules on PCB; Reflector; Outer lens; rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of each function on left and right lamps at the prescribed test points; pass if intensity distributions are substantially identical (not required for a matched pair).

text: In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle and only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the front of the vehicle.
applies_to: Outer lens; Housing (manufacturer logo, if incorporated)
test_case: Visual inspection of vehicle rear and front; pass if at most one logo per side or one central logo is incorporated in lamps on each of the rear and front.

text: All logos incorporated in lamps that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
applies_to: Outer lens; Housing (manufacturer logo, if incorporated)
test_case: Visual inspection of lamp logos; pass if any logo is solely a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo.

text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the requirements of the preceding paragraphs on the installation of lighting and light-signalling devices shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
applies_to: Installation of rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector) on the vehicle
test_case: Installation inspection per UN R48: if the vehicle's external shape is asymmetrical, check lamp positioning and symmetry against the preceding installation requirements. Pass if they are met, or if any deviation is caused only by the asymmetrical body shape and is kept to the minimum possible.

text: Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector in a single housing)
test_case: Inspection of the installed lamp and verification against each applicable colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility and electrical connection requirement of UN R48 for every grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated function; pass if all are met.

text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions; LED modules; outer lens
test_case: Photometric and colorimetric measurement of each function individually with all other grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated functions switched OFF; pass if each meets its photometric and colour requirements.

text: When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.
applies_to: Rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with stop lamp (or other functions); outer lens
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of each reciprocally incorporated function with that function and the rear position lamp switched ON simultaneously; pass if the colour of each function remains within its specified chromaticity limits.

text: Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are not permitted to be reciprocally incorporated.
applies_to: Stop lamp function unit
test_case: Design review/inspection of the lamp: verify the stop lamp does not share illuminating surface/light source/body in a reciprocally incorporated manner with any direction-indicator lamp; pass if not reciprocally incorporated.

text: Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.
applies_to: Stop lamp function unit when grouped with a direction-indicator lamp; outer lens
test_case: Project apparent surfaces onto a plane perpendicular to the reference axis and check any horizontal or vertical line; pass if no line crosses more than two colour borderlines.

text: Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, based upon the areas bounded by the outline of their light emitting surfaces, shall not overlap.
applies_to: Stop lamp function unit when grouped with a direction-indicator lamp
test_case: Drawing/geometric check of apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis; pass if no overlap.

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis. These requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions with segmented apparent surfaces; outer lens (retro-reflector exempt)
test_case: Geometric analysis of apparent surface projection in direction of the reference axis: pass if filled area ≥ 60 % of circumscribing quadrilateral, or gap between facing edges ≤ 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
applies_to: Lamp functions marked "D"; retro-reflectors where two independent units form a single lamp
test_case: Geometric analysis of the two apparent surfaces in direction of reference axis: pass if ≥ 60 % of circumscribing quadrilateral, or facing-edge distance ≤ 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
applies_to: Rear position and stop lamp functions forming an interdependent lamp system
test_case: Geometric analysis per paragraph 5.7.2.1 (≥ 60 % fill of circumscribing quadrilateral or ≤ 75 mm gap between facing edges).

text: Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system; however, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
applies_to: Housing and outer lens containing multiple functions/apparent surfaces
test_case: Design review: verify that lamps/apparent surfaces sharing the same housing or common outer lens are not declared as an interdependent lamp system unless band/strip-shaped.

text: Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
applies_to: Band/strip-shaped lamp functions; vehicle installation
test_case: Measurement on vehicle: symmetry about median longitudinal plane, distance to extreme outer edge ≤ 0.4 m on both sides, length ≥ 0.8 m.

text: The illumination of a band- or strip-shaped lamp surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.
applies_to: LED modules on PCB of band/strip-shaped lamp functions
test_case: Inspection of light source layout: pass if at least two light sources are located as close as possible to the ends of the band/strip.

text: The light-emitting surface of a band- or strip-shaped lamp may be constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements on condition that these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
applies_to: Outer lens and LED modules of band/strip-shaped lamp functions
test_case: Project juxtaposed light-emitting elements onto a transverse plane; pass if ≥ 60 % fill of circumscribing quadrilateral or gaps ≤ 75 mm per paragraph 5.7.2.1.

text: Where the (maximum and minimum) height of the lamp above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation height
test_case: Inspection of vehicle installation: if the lamp height is clearly within the R48 limits with margin, confirm acceptance without exact edge determination of the apparent surface.

text: Where the position of the lamp as regards width clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp lateral position
test_case: Inspection of vehicle installation: if lateral position is clearly within R48 limits with margin, confirm acceptance without exact edge determination.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, LED modules on PCB, outer lens
test_case: Switch each function ON at nominal voltage and monitor luminous intensity, colour and apparent surface over the ON period; pass if no intentional variation occurs (only variations permitted under paragraph 5.9.2).

text: Direction-indicator lamps, the vehicle-hazard warning signal, amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7., and the emergency stop signal shall be flashing lamps.
applies_to: Stop lamp (where used to provide the emergency stop signal)
test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal (if provided via the stop lamps) and verify that the lamp operates in flashing mode according to paragraph 6.23.1.

text: The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp (e.g. position/stop shared LEDs)
test_case: For each permitted variation condition implemented (ambient light, other lamps ON/OFF, combined function), measure photometry in each state; pass if each state complies with the photometric/colorimetric provisions of the lamp's component regulation.

text: Answer-back signal may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or vary in apparent surface; the lamp(s) used for answer-back signal shall operate according to the conditions specified in the general specifications and/or in paragraph 6.27.
applies_to: Rear position lamp / stop lamp if used for answer-back signal
test_case: If the lamp is used for the answer-back signal, activate the signal in park condition and verify operation conforms to the general specifications and paragraph 6.27.

text: Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp; retro-reflector; outer lens
test_case: Vehicle-level visibility check per paragraph 5.10.4.1 (Zone 1, transverse plane 25 m in front, Annex 4); pass if no red light from the rear lamp is visible from the front.

text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
applies_to: Rear position lamp; stop lamp; retro-reflector; housing and outer lens geometry; installation on vehicle
test_case: Geometric/CAD or physical sightline check per Annex 4: observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle; pass if no part of the apparent surface of any red lamp is directly visible.

text: For the visibility of white light towards the rear of a vehicle, with the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).
applies_to: Reversing lamp (exempted); any white light from the rear combination lamp
test_case: Sightline check per Annex 4: observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane 25 m behind the vehicle; pass if no apparent surface of a white lamp other than reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings is directly visible.

text: The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
applies_to: rear position lamp; LED modules on PCB; connector / vehicle wiring harness
test_case: Vehicle installation inspection and functional check: operate the lighting switch in all positions and verify that the rear position lamp is never ON while the front position lamps, the end-outline and side-marker lamps (if fitted) or the rear registration plate lamp are OFF, and vice versa. Pass if all switch ON and OFF simultaneously.

text: The requirement that the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps and rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously does not apply while front and rear position lamps, as well as side-marker lamps when combined or reciprocally incorporated with said lamps, are switched ON as parking lamps.
applies_to: rear position lamp; vehicle wiring harness
test_case: Functional check with parking lamp function activated: verify that non-simultaneous switching occurs only in parking lamp mode. Pass if the deviation from simultaneous switching is limited to this condition.

text: The requirement that the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps and rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously does not apply while side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators.
applies_to: rear position lamp; vehicle wiring harness
test_case: Functional check with direction indicators operating: verify that any non-simultaneous switching is limited to side-marker lamps flashing in conjunction with direction indicators.

text: The requirement that the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps and rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously does not apply while daytime running lamps are switched ON.
applies_to: rear position lamp; vehicle wiring harness
test_case: Functional check with daytime running lamps switched ON: verify that any non-simultaneous switching of the position lamp group occurs only under this condition.

text: The requirement that the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps and rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously does not apply while the front position lamps function is substituted under the provisions of paragraph 5.12.1.
applies_to: rear position lamp; vehicle wiring harness
test_case: Functional check with front position lamp function substituted per paragraph 5.12.1.: verify that any non-simultaneous switching occurs only under this condition.

text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
applies_to: rear position lamp; stop lamp; reversing lamp (function units, if designed as interdependent lamp system); LED modules on PCB
test_case: Where any function is an interdependent lamp system: activate and deactivate the function and verify (visually or by current/photometric measurement on each unit) that all light sources of all interdependent lamps switch ON and OFF simultaneously.

text: Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed by this Regulation (e.g. for the position lamps), it may be replaced by an "operating" tell-tale.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit) – associated driver tell-tale on vehicle
test_case: Vehicle inspection: identify each function for which a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed; verify a tell-tale is fitted that indicates at least that the device is switched ON (closed-circuit), or an operating tell-tale is fitted instead. Pass if one of the two is present and functional.

text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function unit); outer lens; LED modules
test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) of the reversing lamp light output by colorimetry/spectroradiometry with the lamp energised at nominal conditions through the outer lens; pass if the coordinates lie within the white chromaticity boundaries defined in the regulation.

text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function unit); outer lens; LED modules
test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) of the stop lamp light output through the outer lens with the lamp energised at nominal conditions; pass if the coordinates lie within the red chromaticity boundaries defined in the regulation.

text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit); outer lens; LED modules
test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) of the rear position lamp light output through the outer lens with the lamp energised at nominal conditions; pass if the coordinates lie within the red chromaticity boundaries defined in the regulation.

text: The colour of the light reflected by a non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (passive conspicuity)
test_case: Illuminate the rear retro-reflector with standard illuminant A and measure the chromaticity coordinates of the reflected light; pass if the coordinates lie within the red chromaticity boundaries defined in the regulation.

text: The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector functions of the rear combination lamp as installed on the vehicle
test_case: Inspection of the vehicle installation: count the installed rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors and compare each count against the number specified in the individual specifications of UN R48 (paragraph 6) for the vehicle category; pass if every count equals the specified number.

text: Any lamp may be installed on movable components provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector) if mounted on a movable component such as a tailgate or boot lid
test_case: Installation inspection: if any function of the rear combination lamp is mounted on a movable component, verify compliance with the conditions of paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. Pass if all conditions are met; otherwise the lamp shall be mounted on a fixed part of the vehicle.

text: Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit); Retro-reflector; installation on movable component (e.g. tailgate/boot lid)
test_case: Installation check on vehicle: place movable component in each fixed position (closed and every fixed open position); verify mounting position, geometric visibility angles, colour and photometric values of rear position lamp and retro-reflector per UN R48 and device regulation. Pass: all requirements met at every fixed position.

text: In the case where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D" (see paragraph 2.4.11.1.), only one of the lamps needs to meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable components.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit); Retro-reflector; installation on movable component
test_case: Check "D" marking on both lamps of the assembly; with movable component in each fixed position, verify that at least one of the two lamps meets the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements. Pass: at least one lamp compliant at every fixed position.

text: Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components where additional lamps for these functions are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, provided that these additional lamps satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit); Retro-reflector; additional lamps on fixed body; electrical switching
test_case: Open movable component to each fixed open position; verify additional lamps are switched ON automatically and measure their position, geometric visibility and photometric performance. Pass: additional lamps ON in every fixed open position and meet all applicable requirements.

text: Where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are obtained by an interdependent lamp system mounted completely on the moving component(s), the lamps shall, at all fixed positions of the movable components, meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps; however, additional lamps for these functions may be switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, provided that these additional lamps satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit); interdependent lamp system on movable component
test_case: With the complete interdependent lamp system on the movable component, test position, geometric visibility, colour and photometry at each fixed position; if additional lamps are used, verify they switch ON in every fixed open position and meet all those requirements. Pass: compliance at all fixed positions.

text: Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector functions (with the exception of direction indicator lamps) are obtained by an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function unit); interdependent lamp system split between fixed body and movable component
test_case: Identify interdependent lamp(s) specified in device approval; at each fixed position of the movable component verify position, outward geometric visibility, colour and photometric values. Pass: all requirements met at every fixed position.
